slides.caption: max compares the two values and returns the larger.
With equal values it returns the second one. For floats use f64::max, because floats are not Ord.
min returns the smaller value. For strings, "smaller" means earlier in alphabetical (byte) order.
Uppercase letters sort before lowercase ones in this order: "Z" < "a".

reverse.title: How Ordering::reverse works
reverse.description: Flips Less and Greater, for sorting in reverse.

slides.caption: reverse turns "a comes first" into "b comes first".
Same as b.cmp(a). For keys: sort_by_key(|x| std::cmp::Reverse(*x)).

then.title: How Ordering::then works
then.description: Uses a second comparison when the first one is Equal.

note.text: by age (oldest first), then by name

slides.caption: then only matters for ties: equal ages are ordered by name.
al and bo are both 30: tied, so names decide: al before bo.
then_with takes a closure, so the second comparison only runs on ties.

note.text: any type that can be ordered

slides.caption: max compares the two values with cmp and returns the larger one.
If both are equal, max returns the second one. For floats use f64::max.
min compares the two values and returns the smaller one.
For a whole list use iter().min(), which returns an Option.

clamp.title: How Ord::clamp works
clamp.description: Keeps a value inside a range [min, max].

slides.caption: Values below min become min; values above max become max.

int_clamp.title: How clamp works for integers
int_clamp.description: Keeps a number between a lower and an upper limit.

slides.caption: clamp(lo, hi) is x.max(lo).min(hi) in one call.
It panics if lo > hi. Floats have their own f64::clamp.

int_cmp.title: How cmp works for integers
int_cmp.description: Compares two numbers: Less, Equal or Greater.

slides.caption: cmp returns an Ordering, which a match can handle completely.
match guess.cmp(&secret) { Less => ..., Greater => ..., Equal => ... } is the classic guessing-game loop.

int_partial_cmp.title: How partial_cmp works for integers
int_partial_cmp.description: cmp wrapped in Some: integers can always be compared.

slides.caption: partial_cmp returns an Option because some types (floats with NaN) cannot always be compared. Integers always can.

int.title: How == works for numbers
int.description: PartialEq::eq: true when both values are the same.

slides.caption: Writing a == b calls eq behind the scenes.
Different number types cannot be compared directly: 4i32 == 4i64 does not compile; convert one first.

is_lt.title: How Ordering::is_lt works
is_lt.description: true if the Ordering is Less.

slides.caption: The is_* methods turn an Ordering back into a yes/no question.
is_le, is_gt, is_ge, is_eq and is_ne exist too.

is_le.title: How Ordering::is_le works
is_le.description: true if the Ordering is Less or Equal.

is_gt.title: How Ordering::is_gt works
is_gt.description: true if the Ordering is Greater.

slides.caption: Useful when you already have an Ordering from a custom comparison.

is_ge.title: How Ordering::is_ge works
is_ge.description: true if the Ordering is Greater or Equal.

is_eq.title: How Ordering::is_eq works
is_eq.description: true if the Ordering is Equal.

is_ne.title: How Ordering::is_ne works
is_ne.description: true unless the Ordering is Equal.

slides.caption: is_ne is true for Less and for Greater.

then_with.title: How Ordering::then_with works
then_with.description: A tie-breaker that is only computed when needed.

slides.caption: then_with runs its closure only when the first comparison is Equal.
ann and al are both 30: the names decide, al before ann.
then takes a ready Ordering; then_with avoids computing it when not needed.

max_by_key.title: How cmp::max_by_key works
max_by_key.description: The larger of two values, compared by a key.

slides.caption: Each value is turned into a key; the keys are compared.
min_by_key, max_by and min_by work the same way. For more than two values use the Iterator versions.

min_by_key.title: How cmp::min_by_key works
min_by_key.description: The smaller of two values, compared by a key.

slides.caption: The keys are the lengths: 4 and 3.
On a tie, min_by_key returns the first value.

max_by.title: How cmp::max_by works
max_by.description: The larger of two values, using your own comparison.

slides.caption: The closure returns an Ordering for the two values.
Same as std::cmp::max, but works for types without Ord, like f64.

min_by.title: How cmp::min_by works
min_by.description: The smaller of two values, using your own comparison.

slides.caption: Only the second field is compared.
So the second pair is returned.
